task_instance: Detect a React 19.1.0 project from package.json, look up the official React docs for the recommended form-pending-state pattern (useActionState), implement a small AddNameForm.jsx component following that documented API, cite the source with a URL and quote in code comments, and verify the component actually builds and renders with the real react/react-dom packages.
evidence: Created package.json declaring react/react-dom 19.1.0 (stack detection step). Attempted WebFetch of https://react.dev/reference/react/useActionState and even https://example.com; both returned EGRESS_BLOCKED from the sandbox's network proxy, so direct doc-page fetching was unavailable. Fell back to WebSearch (queries: 'react.dev useActionState reference' and '"useActionState" "isPending" example code addNewName React 19'), which surfaced official react.dev snippets confirming the signature `const [state, formAction, isPending] = useActionState(fn, initialState)` and its purpose/pending-state semantics, with react.dev URLs as sources. Wrote AddNameForm.jsx implementing this documented pattern (form + useActionState + isPending-driven disabled/label state), with source citation (https://react.dev/reference/react/useActionState) and an explicit UNVERIFIED note flagging that the exact quoted sentence came from search snippets rather than a direct page fetch, per the skill's citation/honesty rules. Ran `npm install react@19.1.0 react-dom@19.1.0 esbuild` (npm registry is allow-listed through the proxy), compiled AddNameForm.jsx with esbuild (jsx=automatic) to AddNameForm.cjs, then rendered it with real react-dom/server (`renderToStaticMarkup`) in a node -e script. Output HTML included the expected <form>, <input name="name">, and <button> plus React 19's generated form-action replay script, confirming the useActionState-based component is syntactically and semantically valid against the actual installed React 19.1.0 API. Files: package.json, AddNameForm.jsx, AddNameForm.cjs (build output) in the work directory.
note: Partial degradation observed but did not block the deliverable: WebFetch to arbitrary external documentation domains (react.dev, developer.mozilla.org, example.com) is blocked by this sandbox's egress policy (EGRESS_BLOCKED), so the skill's preferred 'fetch the specific documentation page' step had to be satisfied via WebSearch snippets instead of a direct page fetch. This was disclosed to the user via an explicit UNVERIFIED comment in the generated code, consistent with the skill's own honesty/citation rules.
